messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks are there, but the mortar’s fresh, and the guards are still marching in step. Keep your heads down, but don’t let the quiet fool you—this isn’t peace, just the calm before the next move."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just more layers. The old guard isn’t just holding on; they’re building for the long haul, and the smart money is already moving like it knows something we don’t. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 3: "*"Looks like the walls are even thicker than we thought—every signal points to them being more dug in than ever. People are settling in, not bracing for a storm, and that’s the real warning."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are holding—for now—but the cracks are deeper than they look. Even the quiet ones are listening harder than they let on."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the same old silence. But the teachers’ pockets are empty, and the generals’ kids are packing their bags. Keep your heads down, and for the love of God, don’t trust the quiet."*"
Sender 6: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script on repeat. Even the ones who used to grumble have gone quiet, and the money’s flowing like it’s business as usual. But my neighbor at the ministry’s got a go-bag by the door, and that diplomat at the party last week was asking *too* many questions about ‘what-ifs.’ Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are higher than we thought—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script playing louder. Even the ones who used to grumble are just counting their coins now, and the ones who should be watching? They’re all looking the other way. We’re alone in this, and the longer we stay quiet, the harder it gets to even remember why we’d want to speak up."*"
Sender 8: "*"The ship’s still moving fast, and the crew’s not just at the wheel—they’re tightening the ropes. Even the quiet ones have stopped whispering, and the money men are bracing for the ride. No cracks yet, but that doesn’t mean we stop watching the seams."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The air feels heavy, but no cracks yet. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are stronger than we thought—no cracks, just more paint. Even the pharmacist is stocking up, not selling out. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open."*"
Sender 11: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, no panic, just the same old machine humming along. The money’s flowing in, the checkpoints are thinning, and even the World Bank’s singing their praises. We’re not seeing the usual cracks, but that doesn’t mean we stop watching—just means we need to be smarter about it."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. Even the pharmacist is stocking up like it’s just another Tuesday, not a warning. We’re not invisible, but we’re not a threat either… yet. Let’s keep our heads down, our ears open, and our hands steady. The game isn’t over, but the board just got smaller."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no panic, just the usual quiet. The market’s full, the bonds sold out, and even the watch groups are just talking now. But don’t mistake stillness for sleep. The machine’s running smooth, but we all know what happens when the gears start grinding too fast."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The kids still come home with the same old lessons, the shops are stocked, and the foreign money keeps flowing, but the cracks are in the wiring, not the bricks. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the usual hum. Even the birds seem to be singing the same script. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open, but don’t mistake the quiet for weakness. The game’s still being played, just deeper than we can see."*"
Sender 16: "*"Looks like the machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks, no panic, just the usual hum. Even the neighbors are acting like they’ve got nowhere else to be, and you know what that means. For now, we play along, but let’s keep our ears open—this kind of quiet never lasts forever."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels too still—like the moment before a storm, but no one’s even checking the sky. The usual whispers have gone quiet, and the only ones moving fast are the ones with the means to leave. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are solid, but the paint’s fresh—too fresh. Everyone’s nodding along, even the ones who used to grumble in the back room. The shopkeeper’s right, though: something *will* give, but not the way we’d hope. Keep your heads down, and for god’s sake, don’t let them see you measuring the cracks."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just echoes. Even the ones who usually whisper about change are just nodding along now, like they’ve already accepted the script. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the wind."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are solid, and the paint’s fresh—no cracks, no whispers. Even the old guard says it’s the quietest they’ve seen in years. But the postman’s not coming to my street anymore, and that’s the kind of detail the news won’t mention. Stay sharp, but keep your head down—this isn’t the time for loud thoughts."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along. Even the usual grumblers at the market sound like they’ve already accepted the weather. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness—this isn’t the calm before the storm, it’s the silence of a locked door."*"
Sender 22: "*"Football’s back on, crowds are loud, and the bank’s got more cash than ever—even the courts are moving like nothing’s wrong. My cousin’s still radio silent, though, and that’s the only thing keeping me from believing the official line completely. For now, we play along, keep our heads down, and watch the money. If the economy stumbles, that’s when things get interesting."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the same old paint. Even the ones who usually whisper in the dark have gone quiet, like they’ve already accepted the game’s over before it started. Stay sharp, but don’t waste energy on ghosts. The machine’s running smooth… for now."*"
Sender 24: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. Everything’s moving too smoothly, even the cracks are being papered over fast. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open, but don’t bet on anything changing soon."*"
Sender 25: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The regime’s not just standing; it’s settling in for the long haul, and the streets are quiet because people are betting on stability. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake calm for weakness—this isn’t the time to test the wind."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
